questions.question: Rate your proficiency in business development (1–10).
Rate your proficiency in generating business leads (1–10).
Rate your proficiency in qualifying leads and opportunities (1–10).
Rate your proficiency in identifying and entering new markets (1–10).
Rate your proficiency in developing strategic partnerships (1–10).
Rate your proficiency in managing business relationships with clients (1–10).
Rate your proficiency in prospecting for potential customers (1–10).
Rate your proficiency in pitching products, services, or partnerships (1–10).
Rate your proficiency in business negotiation (1–10).
Rate your proficiency in analyzing competitors and market positioning (1–10).
Rate your proficiency in preparing business proposals (1–10).
Rate your proficiency in identifying account-growth opportunities (1–10).
Rate your proficiency in managing business-development activity in a CRM (1–10).
Rate your proficiency in evaluating revenue opportunities (1–10).
Rate your proficiency in building and managing strategic partnerships (1–10).
How many projects, campaigns, or real work experiences have you completed involving lead generation or prospecting?
How many projects or real work experiences have you completed involving qualification of business opportunities?

options.A: Identify potential customers or business opportunities that may be relevant

questions.question: A company sells specialized software to hospitals. Which prospecting approach is most appropriate?

options.A: Target organizations and contacts that fit the product's relevant industry and use case
options.B: Contact every person on social media
options.D: Send the same message to every possible company without research

questions.question: Why is defining an ideal customer profile useful?

options.A: It helps focus prospecting on organizations or people likely to have relevant needs and fit
options.B: It guarantees every contacted lead will buy
options.C: It removes the need for qualification

questions.question: A prospecting list contains thousands of companies but no information about their size, industry, or relevance. What should happen first?

options.A: Enrich or segment the list using relevant qualification criteria
options.D: Assume every company is equally valuable

questions.question: Which is more useful when assessing a lead source?

options.A: Qualified opportunities generated relative to the effort and cost involved
options.D: Number of names in the database

questions.question: A prospect responds that they are interested but provides no details about their need. What should the salesperson do?

options.A: Ask discovery questions to understand the need, fit, and context

questions.question: Why is personalized prospecting often more effective than completely generic outreach?

options.A: It can connect the message to the prospect's relevant context or problem
options.C: It eliminates the need for a product

questions.question: A lead source produces many leads but almost no qualified opportunities. What should be investigated?

options.A: Lead quality, targeting, qualification criteria, and source relevance
options.B: Only the total number of leads

questions.question: A salesperson wants to prioritize outreach among 100 prospects. Which approach is strongest?

options.A: Rank prospects using fit, need, potential value, intent, and relevant timing
options.B: Contact them in alphabetical order only
options.D: Contact only the companies with the largest logos

questions.question: A student claims substantial prospecting experience. What should they be able to explain?

options.A: How they identified prospects, sourced information, prioritized outreach, contacted them, and measured results
options.C: Only the number of leads generated

questions.question: What is the main purpose of lead qualification?

options.A: Determine whether an opportunity has sufficient fit, need, and potential to justify further effort

questions.question: A prospect needs a problem your product solves, but has no budget and no authority to purchase. What should be investigated?

options.A: The buying process, timing, stakeholders, and whether there is a realistic path to purchase
options.B: Immediately mark the lead as won

questions.question: Which is a useful qualification signal?

options.A: A real business need that fits the product or service
options.C: The prospect's social-media follower count only
options.D: The number of employees with no context

questions.question: A prospect says, "This looks interesting," but cannot identify a problem they need solved. How should the salesperson respond?

options.A: Explore the prospect's current situation and needs before treating it as a qualified opportunity
options.C: Mark it as a high-value deal

questions.question: Why is buying authority relevant during qualification?

options.A: A contact may be interested but not able to approve or influence the purchase sufficiently

questions.question: A qualified opportunity has a strong need and fit but the buyer's timeline is 18 months away. What should the salesperson do?

options.A: Record the timing and plan an appropriate follow-up rather than treating it as an immediate deal

questions.question: What is a qualification framework useful for?

options.A: Apply consistent criteria when evaluating opportunities

questions.question: A prospect fits the industry but has no identifiable need. What should happen?

options.A: Continue discovery before investing heavily in the opportunity

questions.question: Why is timing useful as a qualification dimension?

options.A: It helps determine when an opportunity can realistically progress
options.D: Timing is only relevant after closing

questions.question: A student claims real lead-qualification experience. What should they be able to explain?

options.A: How they evaluated fit, need, authority, timing, value, and next steps for actual prospects

questions.question: What should a strong business pitch primarily communicate?

options.A: The problem, proposed value, evidence, differentiation, and desired next step

questions.question: A pitch contains many product features but never explains the customer's problem. What is the main weakness?

options.A: It focuses on the solution without establishing customer value
options.B: It has too much customer research

questions.question: What should a business proposal normally include?

options.A: Relevant problem, proposed solution, scope, value, assumptions, and commercial or next-step information

questions.question: A prospect asks, "Why should we choose you instead of another provider?" What should the response focus on?

options.A: Relevant differentiation supported by evidence and tied to the customer's needs

questions.question: Why should a pitch be adapted to its audience?

options.A: Different stakeholders care about different business outcomes, risks, and decision criteria
options.D: A pitch should always use the same language

questions.question: A proposal promises outcomes that the company cannot realistically deliver. What is the main risk?

options.A: Loss of trust and potential delivery or contractual problems

questions.question: What is a good response when a prospect raises a difficult objection during a pitch?

options.A: Understand the concern, clarify it, and respond with relevant evidence or explanation

questions.question: A proposal is technically strong but uses unfamiliar internal terminology. What should be improved?

options.A: Use language appropriate to the audience and decision context
options.D: Increase technical detail regardless of audience

questions.question: A pitch ends without a clear next step. What is missing?

options.A: A specific call to action or agreed follow-up

questions.question: A student claims real pitching experience. What should they be able to explain?

options.A: The audience, problem, pitch structure, objections, value proposition, evidence, and outcome

questions.question: What makes a strategic partnership potentially valuable?

options.A: Both parties can gain meaningful value from complementary capabilities, audiences, resources, or distribution
options.B: The partnership has a long contract only
options.D: One party receives all the value

questions.question: Two potential partners are interested but have different goals. What should be clarified first?

options.A: Shared objectives, responsibilities, value exchange, and success criteria

questions.question: Why is partner fit important?

options.A: Misaligned capabilities, customers, incentives, or strategy can reduce partnership value
options.B: Any two companies are automatically compatible
options.C: Large companies are always better partners
options.D: Partnerships do not require shared value

questions.question: A partner can provide distribution but wants exclusivity. What should the business-development team evaluate?

options.A: Expected value, strategic implications, alternatives, risks, and contractual constraints

questions.question: What is a useful partnership success metric?

options.A: A measurable outcome tied to the partnership's agreed objective

questions.question: A partnership generates activity but no meaningful business results. What should be reviewed?

options.A: Whether the partnership's activities are actually connected to its intended outcomes

questions.question: Why should responsibilities be clearly defined in a partnership?

options.A: To reduce ambiguity around ownership, delivery, and accountability

questions.question: Two teams disagree about how partnership revenue should be attributed. What should happen?

options.A: Define the commercial model and attribution rules explicitly
options.D: Let the larger company decide automatically

questions.question: A strategic partner repeatedly misses its commitments. What should the partnership owner do?

options.A: Review agreed obligations, impact, root causes, and available corrective actions

questions.question: A student claims experience building business partnerships. What should they be able to explain?

options.A: How they identified the partner, established mutual value, negotiated responsibilities, managed execution, and measured results

questions.question: What is an important principle in business negotiation?

options.A: Understand each party's interests, constraints, alternatives, and desired outcomes

questions.question: A customer asks for a large discount with no additional commitment. What should a salesperson consider?

options.A: Whether the concession can be exchanged for value such as volume, term, scope, or commitment

questions.question: Why is an alternative option important in negotiation?

options.A: It affects the leverage and minimum acceptable outcome of a party
options.C: Alternatives only matter after a deal closes

questions.question: What is the purpose of competitive analysis?

options.A: Understand competitors' positioning, capabilities, strengths, weaknesses, and market approach

questions.question: A competitor has a lower price but significantly weaker service levels. What should the business-development team communicate?

options.A: The relevant value difference and why it matters to the customer's priorities
options.B: Only that the competitor is bad

questions.question: An existing customer uses one product but has several adjacent needs. What should the account team do first?

options.A: Understand the customer's needs and identify relevant expansion opportunities
options.C: Increase the customer's price without discussion

questions.question: What is a useful signal for an account-expansion opportunity?

options.A: A newly identified customer need that fits an existing product or service capability

questions.question: Why is accurate CRM data important in business development?

options.A: It supports reliable pipeline visibility, follow-up, forecasting, and account management

questions.question: A sales pipeline contains three opportunities worth ₹2 lakh each with an estimated 50% probability of closing. What is their simple weighted pipeline value?

options.A: ₹3 lakh

questions.question: A student claims experience managing competitive deals or growing customer accounts. What should they be able to explain?

options.A: The customer need, competitive situation, account strategy, commercial decisions, and measurable outcome

questions.question: A CRM contains hundreds of opportunities with no recent updates. What is the most important issue?

options.A: Pipeline data quality and opportunity freshness

questions.question: What is a sales-stage definition useful for?

options.A: Create consistent criteria for understanding where an opportunity is in the process

questions.question: A company has many opportunities but limited sales capacity. Which opportunities should receive greater attention?

options.A: Those with stronger fit, need, value, probability, and timely next steps

questions.question: An existing customer has low product adoption. What should happen before attempting an upsell?

options.A: Understand adoption barriers and customer outcomes

questions.question: Why should pipeline forecasts include probability or confidence estimates?

options.A: Different opportunities have different likelihoods of reaching the expected outcome

questions.question: A company wants to enter a new market through a local partner. What should be evaluated?

options.A: Market demand, partner fit, capabilities, economics, risks, and route to market

questions.question: A potential partner can provide access to customers but has poor operational capability. What should the team consider?

options.A: Whether the expected customer access outweighs execution and reputation risks

questions.question: A company has three possible growth opportunities but resources for only one. What is a strong decision process?

options.A: Compare expected value, strategic fit, resources, risks, and time to impact
options.B: Choose the opportunity with the longest presentation

questions.question: A new opportunity looks large but has no clear customer need or buying process. What should happen?

options.A: Continue discovery before treating the opportunity as strategically attractive

questions.question: A student claims substantial business-development experience. Which question best verifies genuine practical experience?

options.A: Ask them to walk through a real opportunity from prospecting and qualification through pitch, negotiation, relationship management, and measurable outcome
options.B: Ask only which CRM they used
options.C: Ask only how many leads they generated
options.D: Ask only the final deal value
